content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter part of the forecast, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes, then corrects downward — suggest dampening response to recent highs.
- Mean reversion is not fully captured; model often fails to anticipate gradual decline after peaks.
- Forecast horizon 1–3 days shows higher error; longer-term (10+ days) forecasts are more stable but still biased upward.
- Model reacts too slowly to downward trends; underestimates falling prices unless preceded by strong recent decline.
- When true values show strong upward momentum, model lags behind — suggest adding momentum-based adjustment.
- Model often fails to account for seasonal or calendar-based price patterns (e.g., summer dip, winter rise) — consider incorporating time-of-year weights.
